Brian J. Moline, Chair

ORDER 
NOW, the above-captioned matter comes before the State Corporation Commission of 
the State of Kansas ("Commission") for consideration and determination. Having examined its 
files and records, and being duly advised in the premises, the Commission finds and concludes as 
follows: 
I. BACKGROUND 
1. 
On June 14, 2004, Shelley Robertson, Timothy Wyrick, Benjamin E. Thomas, 
and Barbara J. McCandless, et al. filed formal complaints in this matter. The filing consisted of 
four separate formal complaints (collectively, "Formal Complaint"), three of which were 
individually signed by Ms. Robertson, Messrs. Wyrick and Thomas, and the fourth signed by 
Ms. McCandless, et al. (collectively, "Complainants"). Addressing the facts and circumstances 
surrounding their Formal Complaint, Complainants stated the following: "The Company has 
traditionally paid for gas service as a portion of the paid rent. They are now requesting residents 
to pay separately for gas service to the rental company." Additionally, Complainants stated their 
belief that such a practice is not legal. 
2. 
K.A.R. 82-1-220(b) provides that formal complaints filed with the Commission 
shall meet the following conditions: 

(1) 
Fully and completely advise each respondent and the commission as to the 
provisions of law or the regulations or orders of the commission that have been or 
are being violated by the acts or omissions complained of, or that will be violated 
by a continuance of acts or omissions; 
(2) 
set forth concisely and in plain language the facts claimed by the complainant to 
constitute the violations; and 
(3) 
state the relief sought by the complainant. 
K.A.R. 82-1-220(c) further provides that upon the filing of a formal complaint, it is to be 
examined by the Commission to ascertain whether or not the allegations, if true, would establish 
a prima facie case for action by the Commission and whether or not the formal complaint 
conforms to the Commission's regulations. If the Commission determines that the formal 
complaint does not establish a prima facie case for Commission action or does not 
conform to these regulations, the Complainant shall be notified of the defects, and an opportunity 
shall be given to amend the formal complaint within a specified time. 
11. DISCUSSION 
3. 
The purpose of this Order is to notify the Complainants that the Commission has 
examined the Formal Complaint filed in this matter on June 14, 2004 and determines it neither 
conforms to the requirements of K.A.R. 82-1-220(b) set forth in paragraph 2 above nor 
establishes a prima facie case for Commission action pursuant to the requirements of K.A.R. 82- 
1-220(c). The Commission wishes to further inform the complainants of the noted defects; 
provide an opportunity for Complainants to amend the Fomal Complaint correcting the defects; 
and allow Complainants a period of time within which to file an Amended Formal Complaint. 
Complainants' failure to file an Amended Formal Complaint within the time specified will result 
in dismissal of the Formal Complaint. Complainants' amendment of the Formal Complaint may 

be accomplished using a single Formal Complaint forrn styled "AMENDED FORMAL 
COMPLAINT", a copy of which is attached to this Order as Attachment 1. 
4. 
The following are intended as suggestions for Complainants' consideration in 
correcting and amending the defects noted in the Formal Complaint filed June 14,2004: 
(a) 
If the Respondent is DCAL, LLC, d/b/a Mount Vernon Apartments, it should be 
so identified on the appropriate lined space in the caption. Complainants Shelley Robertson, 
Timothy Wyrick, Benjamin E. Thomas, and Barbara J. McCandless, et al. should be named in 
the lined space of the caption for Complainant, as well as in the opening line of the Amended 
Formal Complaint. In addition to the four Complainant's names, their addresses and telephone 
numbers should also be entered in the opening line of the Amended Formal Complaint. The 
word gas should be entered in the lined space for identifying the type of utility service. 
(b) 
In the facts and circumstances portion of the Amended Formal Complaint, 
Complainants should state with more specificity the practices of the Respondent that 
Complainants allege are unlawful, citing the appropriate statute(s) and regulation(s) that 
Respondent is allegedly violating. For example: Respondent is unlawfully acting as a public 
utility providing gas service and separately billing tenants of Mt. Vernon Apartments for gas 
service provided in violation of K.S.A. 66-104. Gas service provided by Respondent to the 
tenants of Mount Vernon Apartments is not separately metered to the individual apartments and 
forms the basis for our complaint under K.A.R. 82-I-220(a) that the rates charged for gas 
service and billed separately from the rent by Respondent are unreasonable, unfair, unjust, 
unjustly discriminatory, unduly preferential and illegal, etc. In support of the Amended Formal 
Complaint, Complainants should submit as exhibits full copies of leases, including addenda, 
fully executed by Respondent and tenant that are currently in effect for any of the Complainants 

signatory to the four formal complaints filed on June 14, 2004, that demonstrate the alleged 
separate billing practices and amounts charged by the Respondent to its tenants for gas service; 
copies of any lease forms, including addenda, provided to Complainants and proposed for use by 
Respondent at Mount Vernon Apartments in the future; as well as copies of any additional 
materials Complainants may possess reflecting Respondent's intended or actual practice of 
separately calculating and billing tenants for gas service. 
(c) 
The Formal Complaint, as filed on June 14, 2004, does not state the relief sought 
by Complainants in the space provided on page 2 under the parenthetical (State action or result 
desired). Complainants must state here the relief sought. For example: ...that Respondent be 
ordered to cease and desist from its practice of billing the tenants of Mount Vernon Apartments 
separately for natural gas sewice, etc. In determining the action or result desired, Complainants 
should be mindful that the Commission has jurisdiction over public utilities, their rates and 
practices, including the distribution and sale of natural gas to the consuming public. The 
Commission has no jurisdiction over landlorditenant issues unrelated to the distribution and sale 
of utility services. 
(d) 
The Amended Formal Complaint should be signed by the four Complainants 
named in paragraph 1 above and their signatures verified before a Notary Public. 
The 
completed, signed and notarized Amended Formal Complaint should be filed within twenty (20) 
days from the date of this Order. The failure of Complainants to file an Amended Formal 
Complaint within the time period specified will result in dismissal of the Formal Complaint. 
111. FINDINGS 
5. 
The Commission finds that the Formal Complaint filed June 14,2004 does not 
conform to the Commission's requirements under K.A.R. 82-1-220(b) and that the allegations of 

the Formal Complaint do not establish a prima facie case for Commission action under K.A.R. 
82-1 -220(c). The Commission further finds that Complainants should be afforded the 
opportunity to amend the Formal Complaint to correct the defects noted and discussed in 
paragraph 4 above. 
IT IS, THEREFORE, BY THE COMMISSION ORDERED THAT: 
A. 
Complainant's Formal Complaint filed in this matter on June 14,2004 does not 
conform to the Commission's requirements under K.A.R. 82-1 -220(b) and the allegations of the 
Formal Complaint do not establish a prima facie case for Commission action under K.A.R. 82-1-
220(c). 
B. 
Complainants may amend the Formal Complaint correcting the defects noted and 
discussed in paragraph 4 above and file their Amended Formal Complaint with the Commission 
within twenty (20) days fiom the date of this Order. Complainants' failure to file an Amended 
Formal Complaint within the specified time period will result in dismissal of the Formal 
Complaint. 
C. 
A party may file a petition for reconsideration of this Order within fifteen (15) 
days from the date of this Order. If service is by mail, service is complete upon mailing, and 
three days shall be added to the above time frame. 
D. 
The Commission retains jurisdiction over the subject matter and the parties for the 
purpose of entering such further order or orders as it may deem necessary. 

BY THE COMMISSION IT IS SO ORDERED.

COMMISSION 
The Consumer Protection Section 
The Consumer Protection section was established by the Kansas 
Corporation Commission (KCC or Commission), in the summer of 1983. 
The Consumer Protection section, officially part of the KCC Office of 
Public Affairs, is responsible for ensuring that all inquiries and complaints 
filed with the KCC are responded to in a complete and timely fashion. 
Additionally, the Consumer Protection section keeps the Commission, 
staff and other interested parties appraised, through periodic reports, of 
the nature and amount of inquiry on complaint filings. 
The Consumer Protection section consists of staff from the Office of 
Public Affairs working with technical staff from other divisions. 
KCC lnformal and Formal Complaint Procedures 
The right of ratepayers to a formal complaint procedure before the KCC is 
guaranteed by statutes K.S.A. 66-101d,e. In compliance with these statutes, 
the KCC established two complaint procedures through which consumers 
may administratively redress utility problems: an informal complaint 
and a formal complaint (K.A.R. 82-1-220). lnformal complaints which 
are not resolved to the satisfaction of the complainant may subsequently 
be processed through the formal complaint procedure without prejudice. 
In fact, the KCC may suggest that an informal complaint be formalized in 
order to assure that a meritorious claim proceeds through the administrative 
process. Occasionally, the KCC has assigned its own staff attorneys to 
represent customer complaints in the formal process which began as an 
informal complaint. 
lnformal Complaint Procedure 
Utility customers may call, write or contact in person the Consumer 
Protection section of the KCC to lodge an informal complaint. An informal 
complaint should be directed to: 
The Kansas Corporation Commission 
Consumer Protection Section 
1500 SW Arrowhead Road, Topeka, Kansas 66604 
785.271.3100 (local) or 1.800.662.0027 (toll free) 
email: public.affairs@kcc.state.ks.us 
lnformal complaints can, for the most part, be handled most effectively by 
telephone. The customer is often seeking a quick solution to a problem he/ 
she is experiencing - a pending disconnection of service, deposit request 
or billing error, for example. The Consumer Protection staff reviews the 
matter with the customer by telephone, making notes of pertinent information. 
The staff then telephones the utility and investigates the complaint. The 
utility responds by checking its records, contacting employees involved, 
reviewing its policies and procedures, etc., and contacting the customer 
to resolve the matter. The utility then reports back to the Consumer 
Protection staff. If the utility and consumer cannot agree on a resolution, 
the Consumer Protection staff will attempt to mediate a mutually agreeable 
solution when possible. 
Sometimes the facts involved dictate that the matter be resolved in writing. 
lnformal complaints initiated by letter should outline the nature of the 
complaint and the appropriate factual information. The complaint is still 
handled informally, but because of more complicated facts, rules and 
regulations involved, or for other reasons, a written format is more desirable. 
In more complex types of complaints, time is sometimes not as vital, 
allowing for written resolutions. Complaints can be received via mail or 
email at the address stated above. 
Formal complaint procedure 
If the Consumer Protection staff is unable to achieve a satisfactory 
resolution, or if the customer is still dissatisfied after the KCC complaint 
staff has approved the utility's response, the customer may file a formal 
complaint. 
The formal complaint is different from the informal complaint in that it: 
Requires formal processing and filing under KCC administrative rules; 
Receives a docket number for KCC processing; 
Is sent to the utility for response; 
Requires the respondent utility to file a written, legal answer within 10 
days after being served with the complaint; 
Requires the KCC to issue an order - even if the matter is 
resolved without hearing; 
May allow the complainant a formal, quasi-judicial evidentiary hearing; 
and 
Allows either party to appeal the KCC decision to District Court. 
The procedure for filing a formal complaint is found in the KCC's rules of 
practice and procedure, published in the Kansas Administrative 
Regulations. (K.A.R. 82-1-201, et seq.) 
The forms for formal complaints are available from the KCC, but individuals 
are free to draft their own complaint pleadings. The formal complaint may 
be filed in person at the KCC's offices, or by mail. When filed by mail, the 
formal complaint should be mailed with an appropriate cover letter. All 
formal complaints, whether filed by mail or delivered in person, must be 
directed to: 
Executive Director 
Kansas Corporation Commission 
1500 SW Arrowhead Road, Topeka, KS 66604 
Do not direct formal complaints to other KCC personnel. 
The procedure used by the KCC in processing formal complaints is as 
follows: 
1. Once the formal complaint has been filed with the Executive Director 
of the KCC, the case is assigned a docket number, and a copy 
of the complaint is served on the respondent utility by the 
KCC after a determination that a prima facie case has been 
established by the complainant. If it is determined that complainant 
has not established a prima facie case, the complaint is returned 
to the complainant, and the complainant is afforded the opportunity 
to amend the complaint. 
2. The respondent 
utility, after receiving the complaint, must 
either answer or satisfy the complainant within 10 days. (K.A.R. 
82-1 -220(d), K.A.R. 82-1 -214(b).) 
3. Upon receipt of the respondent utility's answer, the complaint and 
the answer are reviewed by the KCC staff. 
4. After investigation and review, KCC staff makes its report to 
the Commission recommending appropriate action. 
5. The Commission, after reviewing the complaint, answer and 
its staff's recornmendation(s), has the following options: 
(A) lssue an order granting or denying the complaint. 
(B) lssue an order dismissing the complaint withlwithout 
prejudice - e.g., on grounds of rnootness because customer 
was accorded satisfaction before the utility answered the 
complaint. 
(C) Schedule the matter for an evidentiary hearing. 
(D) lssue such other orders as are appropriate, e.g., subpoena 
utility records for further review, etc.

The above-captioned matter comes before the State Corporation Commission of the State 
of Kansas (Commission) for consideration and determination. Having examined its files and 
records, and being duly advised in the premises, the Commission finds and concludes as follows: 
I.
JURISDICTION AND BACKGROUND
1.
Pursuant to K.S.A. 66-1,111, 66-1,112 and 66-1,114b, the Commission is given full
power, authority and jurisdiction to supervise and control motor carriers, as defined in 49 C.F.R. 
390.5 and as adopted in K.A.R. 82-4-3f, doing business or procuring business in Kansas, and is 
empowered to do all things necessary and convenient for the exercise of such power, authority, 
and jurisdiction. 
2.
Pursuant to K.S.A. 66-1,129a, 66-1,130, and 66-1,142b, the Commission may
suspend operations, revoke, or amend certificates, and initiate sanctions or fines against every 
motor carrier and every person who violates any provision of Kansas law in regard to the regulation 
of such motor carriers and persons, or who fails to obey any order, decision, or regulation of the 
Commission.

II. 
FINDINGS OF FACTS 
3. 
DMK Transport LLC (Carrier) is a motor carrier, as defined in 49 C.F.R. 390.5 
and as adopted in K.A.R. 82-4-3f, which operates commercial motor vehicles in interstate 
commerce under the USDOT Number 3547324. 
4. 
On May 9, 2024, the Commission issued a Penalty Order in this docket assessing a 
$300 civil penalty against Carrier for failure to pay its 2024 UCR fees. 
5. 
Carrier contacted Staff after the issuance of the Penalty Order stating that Carrier 
is no longer operating and requested inactivation of its USDOT Number. 
6. 
Staff inactivated the Carrier’s USDOT Number. Additionally, after reviewing 
available records, Staff could not find evidence the carrier was found operating in interstate 
commerce. Staff therefore determined the Penalty Order issued for not paying their 2024 UCR 
fees should be vacated. 
7. 
On May 13, 2024, Transportation Staff filed its Motion to Vacate Penalty Order 
recommending the Commission vacate the Penalty Order.

8. 
The Commission finds it has jurisdiction over DMK Transport LLC because 
Carrier is a motor carrier as defined in 49 C.F.R. 390.5 and as adopted in K.A.R. 82-4-3f. 
9. 
The Commission further finds that Carrier does not operate in interstate commerce. 
10. 
Therefore the Commission concludes it is appropriate to vacate the Penalty Order 
issued May 9, 2024. 
THE COMMISSION THEREFORE ORDERS THAT: 
A. 
The Penalty Order issued to DMK Transport LLC on May 9, 2024 is hereby 
vacated.

NOW, the above-captioned matter comes for consideration and determination by the State 
Corporation Commission of the State of Kansas ("Commission"). Having examined its files and records, 
and being fully advised in the premises, the Commission finds and concludes as follows: 
1. 
On May 1,200 1, the Commission issued its Order to Show Cause to Silvio Santos, d/b/a 
Caribe Tours, of Kansas City, Kansas ("Mr. Santos") 
directing Mr. Santos to appear before the 
Commission for a Prehearing Conference on June 1 1,200 1, at 10:OO a.m. 
2. 
On June 1 1,200 1, Mr. Santos appeared for the Prehearing Conference. After discussing 
the matter and facts with Staff, the Prehearing Conference was convened on the record. At that time, 
Theresa Marcel Nuckolls, counsel Staff for the Commission ("Staff'), and Mr. Santos jointly moved the 
Commission for a sixty day Suspension of Procedural Schedule. 
3. 
At that time, Mr. Santos indicated that he was no longer operating, and would not do so 
until he could do so in accordance with the law. He stated that he intended to come into compliance with 
all state laws applicable to his operation. Therefore, he parties jointly verbally moved for a sixty day

2001, because it looked as if Mr. Santos was making progress, Staff moved to suspend that scheduIe to 
allow more time for settlement. On August 7, 200 1, the Commission entered an Order suspending the 
Procedural Schedule. 

4. 
On August 22,200 1, the United States Department of Transportation cited Caribe Tours 
with 11 violations of federal law, including operating without proper state or federal authority. 
5. 
The Commission finds and concludes that its suspension of the procedural schedule to 
encourage settlement is no longer likely to result in settlement. 
6. 
The Commission therefore a prehearing conference in this matter shall be held on 
October 23,2001 at 9:3O a.m. in the Commission's Third Floor Hearing Room, 1500S.W. Arrowhead, 
Topeka, Kansas. 
This prehearing will be used to discuss the possibility of settlement, to establish the 
procedure and issues remaining, to set the schedule for a techcal hearing, and any other matters that may 
aid in the disposition of the proceeding. 
8. 
If Mr. Santos, d/b/a Caribe Tours, fails to attend and participate in the prehearing, 
or other stages of the adjudicative proceeding, he may be held in default pursuant to K.S.A. 77-520. 
If such default occurs, a judgment and fine may be assessed against Mr. Santos.

The above-captioned matter comes before the State Corporation Commission of the State 
of Kansas (Commission). Having examined its files and records, and being duly advised in the 
premises, the Commission finds and concludes as follows: 
I.
JURISDICTION
1.
Pursuant to K.S.A 66-1,108b, 66-1,111, 66-1,112g and 66-1,115, the Commission
is given full power, authority and jurisdiction to supervise and control motor carriers, as defined 
in 49 C.F.R. Part 390.5 and adopted by K.A.R. 82-4-3f, doing business or procuring business in 
Kansas, and is empowered to do all things necessary and convenient for the exercise of such power, 
authority and jurisdiction. 
2.
Pursuant to K.S.A. 66-1,129a, 66-1,130 and 66-1,142b, the Commission may
suspend operations, revoke or amend certificates, and initiate sanctions or fines against every 
motor carrier and every person who violates any provision of Kansas law in regard to the regulation 
of such motor carriers and persons, or who fails to obey any order, decision or regulation of the 
Commission. 

2 

3. 
Pursuant to 49 U.S.C. § 14504a, the Unified Carrier Registration (UCR) Act is a 
federally mandated commercial motor vehicle registration program administered by individual 
States for motor carriers self-designating their operations as interstate commerce. Kansas 
administers the UCR Act pursuant to K.S.A. 66-1,139 which requires motor carriers to “register 
their motor vehicles in their base state pursuant to federal statutes.” 49 U.S.C. § 14504a(i)(4) 
expressly authorizes States the ability to issue citations and impose reasonable fines and penalties 
“pursuant to the applicable laws and regulations of the State on any motor carrier, motor private 
carrier, freight forwarder, broker, or leasing company for failure to ...pay the fees required.” 
4. 
UCR fees are set annually by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration 
(FMCSA). The Commission enforces this registration requirement as outlined in the Uniform 
Penalty Assessment Matrix (Penalty Matrix), reviewed each year by July 1 and subsequently 
approved by the Commission. The Penalty Matrix establishes the structure of penalties for failure 
to pay the required UCR fees. 
II. FINDINGS OF FACT 
5. 
On December 2, 2022, Staff submitted a Report and Recommendation (R&R) 
regarding Heartland Masonry Inc’s (Carrier’s) failure to pay its 2022 UCR fees. As part of the 
R&R, Staff recommended the Commission assess Carrier a penalty in the amount of $300, to be 
paid through the Carrier’s Kansas Trucking Regulatory Assistance Network (KTRAN) account, 
and require Carrier to pay its outstanding UCR fees for 2022 through the UCR website at 
www.ucr.gov. A copy of the R&R is attached hereto as Attachment “A” and incorporated herein 
by reference. 
6. 
As noted in the R&R, Carrier has operating authority under United States 
Department of Transportation (USDOT) number 3903951. According to Carrier’s USDOT 

3 
profile,1 it designates itself as an interstate carrier, with its base as State as Kansas. Carrier owns 
5 self-propelled vehicle(s) that meet the definition of the type of vehicle for which Carrier is 
required to pay annual UCR fees.2 
7.
According to Staff’s R&R, multiple attempts were made to contact Carrier
regarding its 2022 UCR fees. The National Registration System (NRS), which is maintained by 
the UCR Board, sent solicitation notices every 15 days beginning February 18, 2022. On June 28, 
2022, a letter was sent to Carrier by Transportation Staff regarding its unpaid 2022 UCR fees.3 
8.
Litigation Counsel for Staff mailed a letter dated August 5, 2022, to Carrier
informing it that it needed to pay its 2022 UCR fees within ten days. Staff advised in the letter 
that nonpayment of UCR fees could result in civil assessments, with a penalty of $300 for each 
instance of non-compliance.4 To date, Commission records indicate that the Carrier has not paid 
its 2022 UCR fees. 
9.
Based on Carrier’s failure to register its commercial motor vehicle(s) for
registration year 2022 and pay the appropriate UCR fees as established in 49 C.F.R. 367, there is 
sufficient evidence to demonstrate that the Carrier is in violation of K.S.A. 66-1,139 in conjunction 
with K.A.R. 82-4-30a, and that a fine in the amount of $300 is warranted. Additionally, Carrier is 
still obligated to pay its 2022 UCR fees through the UCR website at www.ucr.gov. 
III.
CONCLUSIONS OF LAW
10.
The Commission finds it has jurisdiction over Carrier because it is a motor carrier
as defined in 49 C.F.R. Part 390.5, as adopted by K.A .R. 82-4-3f.

carrier, motor private carrier, or freight forwarder.

11.
The Commission finds Carrier committed one violation of K.S.A. 66-1,139 for

SUBJECT: Docket No. 23-TRAM-487-PEN, Heartland Masonry Inc 

Motor Carrier Penalty Order for Failure to Pay 2022 UCR Fees 

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY: 
Heartland Masonry Inc (Carrier) is a carrier that has self-declared to be an interstate motor 
carrier on its USDOT profile. Interstate motor carriers are required to pay annual Unified Carrier 
Registration (UCR) fees. Staff has attempted, without success, to contact Carrier regarding its 
2022 UCR fees. A letter was sent to Carrier by Staff on June 28, 2022. An additional letter dated 
August 5, 2022, was sent by Litigation Counsel for Staff. Also, the National Registration System 
(NRS), which is maintained by the UCR Board, sent solicitation notices every 15 days beginning 
February 18, 2022 to any unregistered motor carriers. To date, Carrier’s profile lists its UCR fees 
for 2022 as unpaid. Staff recommends Carrier be assessed a penalty for failure to complete its 
federal registration as required by K.S.A. 66-1,139, as outlined in the applicable Uniform Penalty 
Assessment Matrix. Additionally Staff recommends the Carrier be required to pay the unpaid 2022 
UCR fees. 

BACKGROUND: 
Heartland Masonry Inc operates under USDOT number 3903951, domiciled in Kansas at 
5400 NW Arroyo Dr, Topeka, Kansas. Staff UCR Manager Verna Jackson has been tasked with 
ensuring Kansas motor carriers conducting interstate operations have properly paid their UCR fees 
for the calendar year 2022. Based on UCR Manager Jackson’s review of Carrier’s USDOT profile, 
Heartland Masonry Inc is self-declared to be conducting interstate operations. On its most recent 
USDOT Profile update, submitted June 20, 2022, the carrier lists 5 vehicle(s). However, its UCR 
fees for 2022 remain unpaid. A copy of the Carrier’s most recent USDOT Profile update is attached 
hereto as Exhibit 1. 

2 
A letter was sent to Carrier by Staff on June 28, 2022. A copy of that letter is attached 
hereto as Exhibit 2. Another letter dated August 5, 2022, was sent by Litigation Counsel for Staff 
also reminding Carrier that its 2022 UCR fees were outstanding, and warning that nonpayment 
would result in the issuance of a penalty order. A copy of this letter is attached hereto as Exhibit 
3. 
Therefore, Staff recommends Carrier be assessed a civil penalty for failure to pay 2022 
Unified Carrier Registration (UCR) fees as required. This is a violation of K.S.A. 66-1,139 for 
failure to “register their motor vehicles in their base state pursuant to federal statutes,” namely 49 
USC 14504a. Additionally, Staff requests the Commission require the Carrier to pay its UCR fees 
for 2022 through the UCR website at www.ucr.gov. 
DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS: 
K.S.A. 66-1,139 requires “all interstate regulated public motor carriers of property, of 
household goods, or of passengers who operate a motor vehicle in Kansas shall register their motor 
vehicles in their base state pursuant to federal statutes” unless otherwise exempted. The UCR Act, 
pursuant to 49 USC 14504a, establishes the registration requirements for motor carriers operating 
in interstate commerce. 
The UCR Act is a federally mandated commercial motor vehicle registration program 
administered by individual states for motor carriers self-designating their operations as interstate 
or are discovered to be operating in interstate commerce through roadside inspections or an 
accident. UCR funds are used by states for administration of the UCR program and enforcement 
of motor carrier safety programs. 
UCR fees are collected from all motor carriers or other entities required to obtain an 
Interstate USDOT number and/or is required to register with the Federal Motor Carrier Safety 
Administration (FMCSA). There are six fee categories and the registration fees are based on the 
number of commercial motor vehicles operated in interstate commerce. 
Kansas based motor carriers can register UCR by logging into the NRS portal at 
www.ucr.gov and paying the UCR fees. 
For the purposes of determining UCR fees, a Commercial Motor Vehicle (CMV) is defined 
as: a self-propelled vehicle used on the highways in commerce principally to transport passengers 
or cargo (as defined under 49 U.S.C. Section 31101), if the vehicle: 
(1) Has a gross vehicle weight rating or gross combination weight rating or gross vehicle
weight or gross combination weight of at least 10,001 pounds, whichever is greater;
(2) Is designed to transport more than 10 passengers including the driver; or
(3) Is used in transporting material found by the Secretary of Transportation to be
hazardous under 49 U.S.C. Section 5103 and transported in a quantity requiring placarding
under regulations prescribed by the Secretary.
The operation of certain non-CMV vehicles still qualify it for UCR fees, but at the lowest 
UCR fee bracket. For example, for lightweight passenger vehicles that do not meet the above 

3 

definition of CMV (l less than 10 passengers including the driver), the fleet size for the UCR 
purposes would be zero and the carrier would register and pay the lowest fee bracket.

The above-captioned matter comes before the State Corporation Commission of the State 
of Kansas (Commission) for consideration and decision. Having examined its files and records, 
and being duly advised in the premises, the Commission makes the following findings: 
1. 
In its Order of April 30, 1984 in Docket No. 127,140-U, the Commission found 
that resellers were public utilities and subject to Commission regulation. As part of that 
regulation, the Commission directed resellers of telecommunications services to file applications 
for Certificates of Convenience and Authority and accompanying tariffs for approval. 
2. 
In its Order of March 21, 1994 in Docket No. 187,168-U, the Commission 
adopted revised streamlined rules and regulations governing resellers and interexchange carriers, 
designed to reflect changes occurring in the marketplace. 
3. 
On May 13, 2005, Comcast Phone of Kansas, L.L.C. (Comcast) filed the above- 
captioned application for a Certificate of Convenience and Authority to engage in the business of 
an interexchange services provider throughout the State of Kansas. Comcast proposes to provide 
interexchange long distance services to residential and business customers. 

4. 
On June 9, 2005, Commission staff (Staff) filed a memorandum recommending 
that the Commission grant Comcast's application. Staff suggested that Comcast be advised that 
it may not provide these services until a tariff has been filed with and approved by the 
Commission. 
5. 
Comcast is a Pennsylvania incorporated company properly registered with the 
office of the Kansas Secretary of State as a foreign corporation authorized to engage in business 
in Kansas and has an "active and in good standing" status with the Secretary's office. 
6. 
To the extent that Comcast's presence in Kansas would increase consumers' 
options for intrastate long distance services, Staff believes the general public would benefit from 
Commission approval of this application. 
7. 
The Commission finds and concludes that the public convenience will be 
promoted by increased options for interexchange long distance services by granting Comcast 
Phone of Kansas, L.L.C.'s application. The Commission, therefore, finds and concludes that 
Comcast Phone of Kansas, L.L.C. should be granted the authority requested in this docket. 
Comcast Phone of Kansas, L.L.C. should be advised that prior to providing service, a tariff must 
be filed with and approved by the Commission. 
IT IS, THEREFORE, BY THE COMMISSION ORDERED AND CERTIFIED THAT: 
A. 
The application of Comcast Phone of Kansas, L.L.C. for a Certificate of 
Convenience and Authority to transact business as a provider of interexchange 
telecommunications services within the State of Kansas is hereby granted pursuant to K.S.A. 66-
131, as set out in the above order. 
B. 
Prior to providing service, a tariff from Comcast Phone of Kansas, L.L.C. must be 
filed with and approved by the Commission. In addition, Comcast Phone of Kansas, L.L.C. is 

hereby reminded of its ongoing obligation to provide telephone relay services to its customers 
under the terms and conditions set forth in this order and under Kansas law. 
C. 
The parties have fifteen days, plus three days if service of this order is by mail, 
from the date this order was served in which to petition the Commission for reconsideration of 
any issue or issues decided herein. K.S.A. 66-118; K.S.A. 2004 Supp. 77-529(a)(l). 
D. 
The Commission retains jurisdiction over the subject matter and the parties for the 
purpose of entering such further order, or orders, as it may deem necessary. 
BY THE COMMISSION IT IS SO ORDERED AND CERTIFIED.

1. 
On May 24, 2007, Golden Belt Telephone Company (Golden Belt) filed an 
application to replace its local tariffs. 
2. 
On June 21, 2007, the Commission suspended this docket in order to allow 
additional time for Golden Belt to respond and identify the rate changes being introduced and 
permit Staff time to analyze the changes. 
3. 
On August 16, 2007, the Commission staff (Staff) submitted its memorandum 
recommending Commission approval of Golden Belt's tariff changes. Staff stated that Golden 
Belt submitted a complete refomat of its General Exchange, Local Exchange, and Message 
Telephone Service Tariffs, making Golden Belt's tariffs more consistent with industry practice 
and standards. The new tariffs will provide a better organized document to represent Golden 
Belt's services and rates. The new tariffs also eliminate duplicate and out dated text. 
4. 
Staff stated that in addition to reorganizing the tariffs for better clarity, some rate 
changes were also being introduced. Under custom calling features many rates remained 

unchanged, while several were reduced by 50 percent. Several service charges were adjusted; 
the biggest change was for premise visits. The premise visit change was adjusted from $25.00, 
established in 1982, to $40.00. The rate of $40.00 is improved over the previous proposed 
premise visit rate of $75.00. The $40.00 charge is comparable with the charges of United 
Telephone Company of Kansas d/b/a Embarq and Southwestern Bell Telephone Company for 
similar services. 
5.

monthly rate was eliminated, saving residential and business customers $24.00 a year in monthly 
charges. 
6. 
Staff further stated that the rate changes submitted by Golden Belt are similar to 
other exchange carrier's regulated rates for comparable services. 
7. 
The Commission finds and concludes that Golden Belt's application to replace its 
local tariffs should be approved.

The application of Golden Belt Telephone Company to replace its local tariffs is 
hereby approved.

any issue or issues decided herein. K.S.A. 66-118; K.S.A. 2006 Supp. 77-529(a)(1).

title: KCC Order — Docket 05-NLPC-452-KSF: Order No. 3:  Accepting Audit and Directing NOSVA to Comply.
text:
Before Commissioners: 
Brian J. Moline, Chair 
Robert E. Krehbiel 
Michael C. Moffet 
In the Matter of the Audit of NOSVA Limited 
1 
Parnership for KUSF Purposes, Year Seven, 
) Docket No. 05-NLPC-452-KSF 
Pursuant to K.S.A. 66-2010(b)(l). 
1 
ORDER NO. 3 
ACCEPTING AUDIT AND DIRECTING NOSVA TO COMPLY 
NOW, the above-captioned matter comes on before the State Corporation 
Commission of the State of Kansas (Commission) for consideration and decision. After 
reviewing its files and records, and being duly advised in the premises, the Commission 
finds and concludes as follows. 
I. Background 
1. 
Pursuant to K.S.A. 66-2002(b) and K.S.A. 66-2008, the Commission 
established the Kansas Universal Service Fund (KUSF) in its December 27, 1996 Order 
in Docket No. 94-GIMT-478-GIT. The National Exchange Carrier Association (NECA) 
was selected through a bidding process to serve as KUSF administrator. 
2. 
Under K.S.A. 66-2010(b)(l), the KUSF administrator is responsible for 
auditing all telecommunications service providers that receive funds from or provide 
funds to the KUSF. 
11. Findings of Fact and Conclusions of Law 
3. On December 3, 2004, the Commission issued Order 1 : Directing NECA to 
Commence an Audit of NOSVA Limited Partnership (NOSVA) for KUSF Purposes. In 

that Order, NECA was instructed to file a report in this docket containing the results of 
the audit and any recommendations that it might suggest. NOSVA would be permitted 
ten days from the file date of the report to file its response, pursuant to K.A.R. 82-1- 
218(d) and 82-1 1-217(c). 
4. Having been granted an extension of time by the Commission, NECA filed its 
final audit report on August 31, 2005, detailing material deficiencies found during the 
audit: 
(a) NOSVA billed some of its customers the KUSF assessment 
on the Presubscribed Interexchange Carrier Charges (PICC) 
and the Service Interruption Protection Plan Charges (SIPP). 
PICC and SIPP are interstate revenues and should not have 
the KUSF charges applied to them. As a result, NOSVA 
overcharged those customers by an amount contained in the 
confidential version of NECA's final audit report. 
NECA recommended that customers should be credited, or 
provided a refund, for the overcharges. The credit or 
refund should include any KUSF assessment on any PIC 
and SJPP revenues charged subsequent to the audit period. 
NECA further recommended that NOSVA's billing be 
modified to prevent such overcharges in the future. 
(b) NOSVA does not report actual intrastate retail revenues, as 
required by the Commission. Instead, NOSVA derives the 
the revenues by dividing the total billed surcharges by the 
surcharge rate. 
NECA recommended that NOSVA complete and submit 
to NECA two true-up forms by September 30,2005-one 
reporting actual revenues for the period of March 2003 
through February 2004 and the other reporting actual 
revenues for the period March 2004 through February 2005. 
NECA further recommended that actual revenues be 
reported on the Carrier Remittance Worksheets (CRWs) on 
a going-forward basis. NECA also reminded NOSVA that 
all intrastate retail revenues should be reported, including 
late payment fees. 
(c) NOSVA maintains its accounting records on a total-company 

basis. Thus, the detail needed to confirm the types or amounts 
of revenues reported to the KUSF was not available. NOSVA 
reported that it was experiencing aggressive competition and 
requested that its consequent downsizing be taken into account. 
NECA noted that NOSVA's billing system appeared to be 
capable of identifying intrastate revenues by type and 
amount. NECA believes that reports generated from this 
billing system should be used to report accurate revenues 
on the CRW and true-up forms. NECA recommends that 
accounting records be set up at the state level so that the 
Kansas revenues can be confirmed in future KUSF reviews. 
(d) Although the annual report revenue did not correspond to 
KUSF revenue, NECA reported that enough back-up 
information was provided to ensure that accurate revenues 
could be determined to for the CRW and true-up forms. 
NECA recommended that the reconciliation section of the 
annual reports be accurately completed in future reporting 
to the Commission. 
More than 10 days have passed since the file date of NECA's audit report and NOSVA 
has not filed comments relative to the report. 
5. The Commission has reviewed NECA's audit report of NOSVA and finds it 
thorough and reasonable. The Commission adopts NECA's recommendations and directs 
NOSVA to (1) refund to, or credit, customers who experienced surcharges applied to 
PICC or SIPP revenues in the amount set out in the confidential version of NECA's 
report, including any such surcharge which occurred after completion of the audit; (2) 
report actual billed intrastate retail revenues on the Carrier Remittance Worksheet on a 
going-forward basis and complete and provide to NECA the two true-up forms described 
above; (3) modify its accounting records to a state level; and, (4) accurately reconcile 
annual reports in the future. NOSVA should advise NECA upon its compliance with the 
foregoing items. 

IT IS, THEREFORE, BY THE COMMISSION ORDERED THAT: 
A. The Commission adopts NECA's filed audit report pertaining to NOSVA 
Limited Partnership and directs NOSVA to comply with the 15 items set forth above.

PENALTY ORDER 
The above captioned matter comes before the State Corporation Commission of the State 
of Kansas. Having examined the files and records, and being duly advised in the premises, the 
Commission finds and concludes as follows: 
I. JURISDICTION 
1. 
K.S.A. 74-623 provides that the Commission has the exclusive jurisdiction and 
authority to regulate oil and gas activities. K.S.A. 55-152 provides that the Commission has 
jurisdiction to regulate the construction, operation, and abandonment of any well and the 
protection of the usable water of this state from any actual or potential pollution from any well. 
The Commission has licensing authority pursuant to K.S.A. 55-155. 
2. 
K.S.A. 55-162 and K.S.A. 55-164 provide the Commission with authority to issue 
a Penalty Order regarding a violation of Chapter 55 of the Kansas Statutes Annotated, or of any 
rule, regulation, or order of the Commission. A Penalty Order may include a monetary penalty of 
up to $10,000, and each day of a continuing violation constitutes a separate violation. 
3. 
K.A.R. 82-3-111 provides that within 90 days after operations cease on any well, 
the operator of that well shall plug the well, return the well to service, or file an application with 
the Conservation Division requesting temporary abandonment ("TA") status. A well shall not be 

eligible for TA status if the well has been shut-in for 10 years or more without an application for 
an exception pursuant to K.A.R. 82-3-100 and approval by the Commission. The failure to file 
an application for TA status shall be punishable by a $100 penalty. K.A.R. 82-3-11 l(e) provides 
an exemption for certain wells for 365 days if they are fully equipped and capable of production. 
II. FINDINGS OF FACT 
4. 
Operator conducts oil and gas activities in Kansas under license number 33960. 
5. 
Operator is responsible for the care and control of the Parker #1-A ("the subject 
well"), API #15-159-21502-00-00, located in Section 33, Township 20 South, Range 6 West, 
Rice County, Kansas. 
6. 
District Staff inspected the subject well and collected evidence indicating it has 
been inactive and unplugged for longer than the 90 days allowed by K.A.R. 82-3-111. The well 
did not appear to be exempt pursuant to K.A.R. 82-3-11 l(e). Operator either did not file a TA 
application or did not bring the well into compliance after a TA application was denied. 
7. 
District Staff sent a letter to Operator, requiring Operator to bring the subject well 
into compliance with K.A.R. 82-3-111 by a deadline. 
8. 
District Staff inspected the subject well after the deadline in the letter passed, 
verifying that the well continued to be inactive and unplugged. 
9. 
District Staff collected evidence and submitted it to the Legal Department with a 
recommendation that the Commission issue this Order. The recommendation sheet submitted by 
District Staff is attached to this Order as Exhibit A, incorporated into this Order, and shall serve 
as the concise and explicit statement of facts required by K.S.A. 77-526. 
2 

III. CONCLUSIONS OF LAW 
10. 
The Commission concludes that it has jurisdiction over Operator and this matter 
under K.S.A. 55-152 and K.S.A. 74-623. 
11. 
The above findings of fact are sufficient evidence to support the conclusion that 
Operator committed one violation ofK.A.R. 82-3-111 because the subject well has been inactive 
in excess of the time allowed by regulation without being plugged, returned to service, or 
approved for TA status. 
THEREFORE, THE COMMISSION ORDERS: 
A. 
Operator shall pay a $100 penalty. 
B. 
Operator shall plug the subject well, return the well to service, or obtain TA status 
for the well if eligible. Obtaining TA status shall include application for, and Commission 
approval of, an exception to the 10-year limit on TA status if applicable. 
C. 
If no party requests a hearing, and Operator is not in compliance with this Order 
within 30 days, then Operator's license shall be suspended without further notice. The notice and 
opportunity for a hearing on this order shall constitute the notice required by K.S.A. 77-512 
regarding license suspension. The Commission may impose further sanctions, including 
additional monetary penalties and any other remedies available to the Commission by law, 
without further notice. 
D. 
Checks and money orders shall be payable to the Kansas Corporation 
Commission. For credit card payments, include the type of card (Visa, MasterCard, Discover, or 
American Express), account number, and expiration date. Payments shall be mailed to the 
Kansas Corporation Commission at 266 N. Main St., Suite 220, Wichita, Kansas 67202. The 
payment must include a reference to the docket number of this proceeding. 
3 

E. 
Any party may request a hearing on the above issues by submitting a written 
request, pursuant to K.S.A. 55-164, K.S.A. 77-537, and K.S.A. 77-542, setting forth the specific 
grounds upon which relief is sought, to the Commission at 266 N. Main St., Suite 220, Wichita, 
Kansas 67202, within 30 days from the date of service of this Order. Hearings will be scheduled 
only upon written request. Failure to timely request a hearing will result in a waiver of 
Operator's right to a hearing. 
F. 
If a party requests a hearing, a corporation or similar entity shall not be permitted 
to enter an appearance except by its attorney. Attorneys for all parties shall enter their 
appearances in Commission proceedings by giving their names and addresses for the record. 
G. 
The Commission retains jurisdiction over the subject matter and the parties for the 
purpose of entering such further order or orders as it may deem necessary. 
BY THE COMMISSION IT IS SO ORDERED.
